'''Thomas "Tom" Stephen Hampden Leinster''' (born 1971) is a British mathematician, known for his work on [[category theory]].

== Education and career ==
Leinster graduated in 2000 with a PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]]. His PhD thesis ''Operads in Higher-Dimensional Category Theory'' was supervised by [[Martin Hyland]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=71356}}</ref> After teaching at the [[University of Glasgow]], Leinster became, and is now, a professor at the [[University of Edinburgh]]. He published textbooks on [[category theory]]<ref>{{cite book|author=Tom Leinster |title=Basic Category Theory |series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |date=2014 |isbn=978-1-107-04424-1 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/basic-category-theory/A72533879BBC7BD956CC415777B7DA99|doi=10.1017/cbo9781107360068 |arxiv=1612.09375 }}</ref> and [[higher categories]] and [[operad]]s.<ref>{{cite book |author=Tom Leinster |title=Higher Operads, Higher Categories |series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |date=2004 |isbn=978-0-521-53215-0 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/higher-operads-higher-categories/E4BC6645A0DA99C2A9D50D8993BA54A9 |doi=10.1017/cbo9780511525896|arxiv=math/0305049 }}</ref> In the 2010s, he was mainly concerned with a generalisation of the [[Euler characteristic]] in category theory, the ''magnitude''. He also considered such generalisations in [[metric space]]s with application in biology (measurement of biodiversity).

== Award and honour ==
[[Leinster group]]s (''i.e.'', [[finite group]]s whose [[order (group theory)|order]] is equal to the sum of the orders of their [[normal subgroup]]s) are named in his honour.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Revisiting the Leinster groups |journal=[[Comptes Rendus Mathematique]] |volume=352 |number=1 |date=January 2014|issn=1631-073X |pages=1–6 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1631073X13003233 |doi=10.1016/j.crma.2013.11.009 |last1=Baishya |first1=Sekhar Jyoti |bibcode=2014CRMat.352....1B |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He received the 2019 [[Chauvenet Prize]] for ''Rethinking Set Theory''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.maa.org/news/maa-to-honor-authors-of-year-s-best-writing-in-mathematics |title=MAA to Honor Authors of Year's Best Writing in Mathematics {{!}} Mathematical Association of America }}</ref> (based upon an [[axiomatisation]] published in 1964 by [[William Lawvere|F. William Lawvere]]).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Lawvere, F. William|title=An elementary theory of the category of sets|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]|volume=52|issue=6|year=1964|pages=1506–1511|doi=10.1073/pnas.52.6.1506|pmid=16591243 |doi-access=free |bibcode=1964PNAS...52.1506L |pmc=300477}}</ref> He is a frequent author and moderator for the academic group blog [[John C. Baez#Forums|''n''-Category Café]], where topics from mathematics, science and philosophy are discussed, often from the perspective of [[category theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/leinster.html |title=Posts by Tom Leinster, The n-Category Café }}</ref> International media attention resulted from a 2014 article by Leinster in the ''[[New Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Tom Leinster |title=Maths spying: the quandary of working for the spooks |journal=New Scientist |volume=222 |number=2966 |date=26 April 2014 |issn=0262-4079 |pages=26–27 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0262407914608277 |doi=10.1016/S0262-4079(14)60827-7|bibcode=2014NewSc.222...26L |url-access=subscription }} [https://slate.com/technology/2014/04/mathematicians-at-the-nsa-and-gchq-is-it-ethical-to-work-for-spy-agencies.html reprint in slate.com]</ref> Leinster's article called, on the basis of ethics, for mathematicians to refuse to work for [[Intelligence agency|intelligence agencies]].<ref>[https://boingboing.net/2014/04/27/mathematicians-refuse-to-work.html Mathematicians: refuse to work for the NSA!], ''[[Boing Boing]]'', 27 April 2014</ref><ref>[https://science.slashdot.org/story/14/04/27/1747230/mathematicians-push-back-against-the-nsa Mathematicians Push Back Against The NSA],
